<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">BUSINESS OVERVIEW</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Centerline Holding Company (OTC: CLNH), through its subsidiaries, provides real estate financing and asset management services focused on affordable and conventional multifamily housing.&#160;&#160;We offer a range of both debt financing and equity&#160;&#160;investment products, as well as asset management services to developers, owners, and investors.&#160;&#160;We are structured to originate, underwrite, service, manage, refinance or sell assets through all phases of its life cycle.&#160;&#160;As a leading sponsor of Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (&#8220;LIHTC&#8221;) funds, we have raised more than $10 billion in equity across 136 funds.&#160;&#160;Today we manage $9.3 billion of investor equity within 116 funds and invest in approximately 1,200 assets located in over 47 U.S. states.&#160;&#160;Our multifamily lending platform services $11.4 billion in loans and mortgage revenue bonds that we manage on behalf of the Federal National Mortgage Association (&#8220;Fannie Mae&#8221;) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (&#8220;Freddie Mac&#8221;), known collectively as Government-Sponsored Enterprises (&#8220;GSEs&#8221;), as well as the Government National Mortgage Association (&#8220;Ginnie Mae&#8221;), and the Federal Housing Administration (&#8220;FHA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Centerline Holding Company, or its predecessor entities, has been in continuous operation since 1972.&#160;&#160;Organized as a statutory trust created under the laws of Delaware, we conduct substantially all of our business through our subsidiaries, generally under the designation Centerline Capital Group.&#160;&#160;The terms &#8220;we&#8221;, &#8220;us&#8221;, &#8220;our&#8221; or &#8220;the Company&#8221; as used throughout this document refer to the business as a whole, or a subsidiary, while the term &#8220;parent trust&#8221; refers only to Centerline Holding Company as a stand-alone entity.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We manage our operations through six reportable segments.&#160;&#160;Our reportable segments include four core business segments and two additional segments: Corporate and Consolidated Partnerships.&#160;&#160;The four core business segments are:&#160;&#160;Affordable Housing Equity, Affordable Housing Debt, Mortgage Banking and Asset Management.&#160;&#160;Our Corporate segment comprises: Finance and Accounting, Treasury, Legal, Marketing and Investor Relations, Operations and Risk Management, supporting our four core business segments.&#160;&#160;In our Consolidated Partnerships segment, we consolidate certain funds we control, notwithstanding the fact that we may have only a minority, and in most cases, negligible, economic interest.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our professional staff has a unique blend of capital markets and real estate expertise, experience, and creativity to provide highly practical, customized solutions for real estate investors, developers, and owners.&#160;&#160;We pride ourselves on our strong underwriting protocols, solid credit processes and procedures, a superior asset management platform, creativity, flexibility, and the ability to react quickly to our customers&#8217; needs.&#160;&#160;We have built a growing debt origination platform with strong sponsor relationships, access to a variety of capital sources, and a stable fund management business with deep investor relationships.&#160;&#160;Most importantly, we have recruited and retained the best professionals to manage, run, and build our businesses.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Business Segments</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Affordable Housing Equity</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our Affordable Housing Equity segment provides equity financing to properties benefiting from the LIHTC or other financial structures (collectively &#8220;Tax Credit&#8221;) intended to promote development of affordable multifamily housing properties.&#160;&#160;The LIHTC program was established as part of the <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Tax Reform Act of 1986</font> to encourage the development of affordable rental housing for low-income families.&#160;&#160;We sponsor and manage funds for institutional and retail investors who invest in affordable housing properties nationwide.&#160;&#160;We have been an industry leader in fund origination and management since inception of the LIHTC program.&#160;&#160;We have raised more than $10 billion in LIHTC equity across 136 LIHTC funds and currently manage $9.3 billion.&#160;&#160;We have provided financing for over 1,600 affordable rental properties located in 47 U.S. states.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Credit Risk Products</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Through Credit Risk Products we provided credit intermediations to facilitate specified rates of return on some of the Tax Credit funds we originated.&#160;&#160;We provide credit intermediations through Centerline Financial Holdings LLC (&#8220;CFin Holdings&#8221;) and its subsidiary, Centerline Financial LLC (&#8220;CFin or Centerline Financial&#8221;), isolated special purpose entities we launched in partnership with Natixis Capital Markets North America Inc. (&#8220;Natixis&#8221;), which currently owns 10% of CFin Holdings, and Centerline Guaranteed Holdings LLC (&#8220;Guaranteed Holdings&#8221;), another isolated special purpose entity.&#160;&#160;Given current market conditions, the immediate outlook is for no new business to be carried out by our Credit Risk Products Group.&#160;&#160;In addition, due to the downgrade of Centerline Financial&#8217;s rating during the second and third quarters of 2010, Centerline Financial has been and continues to be prohibited from providing any new credit intermediations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As of December 31, 2011, due to a wind-down event caused by a capital deficiency under the Centerline Financial operating agreement that occurred in 2010, the Centerline Financial senior credit facility is in default.&#160;&#160;Amounts under the Centerline Financial senior credit facility are still available to be drawn, and we do not believe this default has a material impact on our financial statements or operations.&#160;&#160;Also, as a result of its wind-down event, Centerline Financial is restricted from making any member distributions and is restricted from doing any new business.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Services performed by our Credit Risk Products Group earn income and cash flows from credit intermediation fees from the fund that are generally received in advance and deferred and recognized over the applicable risk-weighted periods, which generally comprise the life of such fund, on a straight-line basis.&#160;&#160;Fees pertaining to the construction and lease-up phase of a pool of properties have income-earning periods that generally last one to five years.&#160;&#160;Fees pertaining to the operational phase of a pool of properties have income-earning periods of approximately 20 years.&#160;&#160;We also earn interest from investing the capital we maintain to support credit intermediations we have issued.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Affordable Housing Debt</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our Affordable Housing Debt segment provides financing to developers and owners of affordable multifamily properties.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We originate and service affordable housing multifamily loans under GSE and FHA programs. In an effort to expand our affordable debt platform and accelerate our production volume, we have recruited a highly experienced FHA and affordable debt team.&#160;&#160;We believe that expanding our affordable debt platform will also provide further expertise and diversification of our product offering which will directly benefit our LIHTC equity business.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our origination staff are long-time veteran&#8217;s in the Affordable Housing Industry with varied backgrounds in investment banking, project management, GSE tenure, and development expertise.&#160;&#160;The composition and geographic disparity of the group creates one of the few nationwide lending platforms and provides clients with national expertise as well as local knowledge.&#160;&#160;Additionally, due to the high level of experience and expertise in the origination, underwriting and credit functions of Affordable Housing debt originations, we enjoy a strong reputation with its lenders and investors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Historically, we acquired mortgage revenue bonds that financed affordable multifamily housing projects, using our balance sheet for the initial acquisition.&#160;&#160;In December 2007, we re-securitized a major portion of our affordable housing mortgage revenue bond portfolio with Freddie Mac, which for accounting purposes was treated as a sale.&#160;&#160;We retained senior Freddie Mac credit-enhanced certificates that collateralize the preferred shares of one of our subsidiaries, a high-yielding residual interest in the portfolio, and servicing rights, as part of the re-securitization transaction.&#160;&#160;As a result of the re-securitization transaction, we earn interest income on the retained certificates, the interest income allocated to the high-yielding residual interest that supports payments under the preferred shares and ongoing servicing fees.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We are currently not acquiring mortgage revenue bonds, although we may resume such acquisitions if/when appropriate investments are available.&#160;&#160;We continue originating, underwriting and servicing mortgage loans for affordable housing properties using the same agency lending programs our Mortgage Banking segment uses for its mortgage originations.&#160;&#160;In most cases, we retain the servicing component on loans we originate, earning servicing fees as well as interest on escrows associated with each loan (for further discussion of agency lending programs and fees earned, see the <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Mortgage Banking</font> section).&#160;&#160;We are currently a Fannie Mae Delegated Underwriting Servicer (&#8220;DUS&#8221;) lender, a FHA Multifamily Accelerated Processing (&#8220;MAP&#8221;) mortgagee, and are in the process of obtaining re-entry into the Freddie Mac Targeted Affordable Housing (&#8220;TAH&#8221;) program, which is expected to be finalized during April 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Mortgage Banking</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our Mortgage Banking segment provides multifamily housing loans for multifamily property types throughout the United States.&#160;&#160;In partnership with our capital sources, primarily GSEs and the FHA, we tailor mortgage products to meet the financing needs of our clients.&#160;&#160;We provide mortgages to Fannie Mae under its DUS program and to Freddie Mac under the Freddie Mac Program Plus (&#8220;Program Plus&#8221;), and previously the Delegated Underwriting Initiative (&#8220;DUI&#8221;) programs.&#160;&#160;Mortgages originated and insured under the FHA programs are typically financed through the sales of mortgage-backed securities guaranteed by Ginnie Mae.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">All loans were closed in our name using cash borrowed from warehousing and repurchase lenders and sold to the GSEs or to the market as Mortgage-Backed Securities (&#8220;MBS&#8221;) guaranteed by Fannie Mae or Ginnie Mae.&#160;&#160;Loan sales were completed within one week to three months following the initial loan closing.&#160;&#160;These transactions are backed by loans we originate and are typically AAA rated securities.&#160;&#160;We use cash from the sale to repay the warehouse and repurchase agreement borrowings.&#160;&#160;We retain no interest in the mortgage loans we originate, although in most cases we do retain the right to service them.&#160;&#160;Mortgage servicing rights are valued and recorded as an asset on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;We also have certain contingent liabilities associated with the shared-risk loans that we originate under the loss-sharing arrangements of the Fannie Mae DUS and Freddie Mac DUI programs (see Note 31 to the consolidated financial statements).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">With respect to our GSE lending program, we earn transaction-based origination fees and trading premiums, recognized upon settlement of the loan sales to the GSE, and earn interest that accrues on loans prior to sale, net of interest expenses on warehoused borrowings.&#160;&#160;We earn servicing fees and various other related fees, including assumption, substitution, modification and prepayment penalties, for loans we service.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">While we have practically no equity interest in the Tax Credit Fund Partnerships and Tax Credit Property Partnerships, we control the operations of these partnerships and therefore consolidate them in our financial statements.&#160;&#160;The assets included in our Consolidated Balance Sheets differs from the amount we refer to as &#8220;Assets under Management&#8221; as the carrying amount primarily reflects mark-to-market adjustments for certain investments and absorption of operating losses for equity investments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Tax Credit Fund Partnerships earn equity income from investments in Tax Credit Property Partnerships.&#160;&#160;Because tax-credit funds are designed to generate tax benefits and losses for their investors, equity income usually is negative and a substantial portion of it is allocated to the investors.&#160;&#160;Tax Credit Property Partnerships earn rental revenues from operating affordable housing properties.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Funding of Operations</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our primary short-term operation needs include payment of compensation and general business expenses, facilitating debt and equity originations, fund management and asset management activities, and funding commitments and contractual payment obligations including debt amortization.&#160;&#160;We fund these short-term business needs primarily with cash provided by operations and asset-backed warehouse credit facilities.&#160;&#160;Our long term liquidity needs include capital needed for potential strategic acquisitions or the development of new businesses, increased financing capacity to meet growth in our businesses, and the repayment of long-term debt.&#160;&#160;Our primary sources of capital to meet long-term liquidity needs include cash provided by operations, term loan and revolver debt.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In October 2011, the parent trust filed an Entity Classification Election (the &#8220;Election&#8221;) with the IRS to become taxable as a corporation in order to achieve tax reporting efficiencies and administrative cost reductions.&#160;&#160;Previously the parent trust was treated as a pass-through entity and all items of income and deductions flowed through to its investors.&#160;&#160;This change in tax status resulted in the parent trust becoming subject to entity-level taxes retrospectively effective July 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;On February 6, 2012, the Company provided investors a final schedule K-1 for the tax period beginning January 1, 2011 and ending July 30, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Regulatory Matters</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The mortgage origination business within our Affordable Housing Debt and Mortgage Banking segments is subject to various governmental and quasi-governmental regulations.&#160;&#160;As noted above, we are licensed or approved to service and/or originate and sell mortgage loans for certain Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac programs.&#160;&#160;Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are federally chartered public corporations that require our subsidiaries to meet minimum net worth and capital requirements and to comply with other reporting requirements.&#160;&#160;Mortgage loans made under these programs are also required to meet the requirements of these programs.&#160;&#160;In addition, under Fannie Mae&#8217;s DUS program we have the authority to originate loans without a prior review by Fannie Mae and are required to share in the losses on loans originated under this program.&#160;&#160;Under the Freddie Mac seller/servicer and TAH programs, we are required to submit loans for review, consideration and final approval with Freddie Mac who takes all of the associated risk on these transactions.&#160;&#160;If they fail to comply with the requirements of these programs, the applicable agency can terminate our license or approval.&#160;&#160;In a very rare occurrence, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac have the authority under their guidelines to terminate a lender&#8217;s authority to originate and service their loans for any reason.&#160;&#160;If our authority is terminated under any of these programs, it would prevent us from originating or servicing loans under that program.&#160;&#160;The parent trust is required to guarantee up to $75 million of such business&#8217; obligations under these programs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Additional Information</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We are subject to competition in all of our business lines, as described in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 1.</font> &#8211; <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Business &#8211; Business Overview &#8211; Competition</font>.&#160;&#160;If competition increases, we may experience compression in the level of profits we earn on our various investments and financing products due to, among other things:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As we may borrow funds to make investments, the ability to access such funds and rising interest rates may compound this issue.&#160;&#160;Absent cost reductions, such compression may not permit us to enjoy the margins we have achieved historically, thereby lowering our revenues and net income.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our assets are pledged and there are restrictions on securitizing/monetizing them</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Substantially all of our assets have been pledged as collateral in connection with our debt facilities and credit intermediation activities and we may not have full access to them until we exit the related programs (see Note 7 to the consolidated financial statements).&#160;&#160;This may prevent us from entering into asset specific financing agreements at terms more favorable than under existing agreements.&#160;&#160;Also, if we are unable to meet the payment terms under the related agreements, we may be forced to sell certain assets, which could result in losses and the elimination of income and cash flows we currently earn.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our Convertible CRA Shares are redeemable and could adversely affect our liquidity</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our Convertible CRA Shares have a redemption feature that can now be exercised.&#160;&#160;We would be required to pay approximately $6.0 million to redeem all of our Convertible CRA Shares, unless we negotiated a settlement with the holders of our Convertible Series A Shares to pay a lesser amount.&#160;&#160;A holder of Convertible CRA Shares with a redemption value of approximately $4.0 million has exercised its option to have those shares redeemed.&#160;&#160;The Credit Agreement contains restrictions on our ability to redeem the Convertible CRA Shares.&#160;&#160;If we are required to redeem our Convertible CRA Shares, it could negatively affect our liquidity.&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 7 &#8211; Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations &#8211; SECTION 3 &#8211; Financial Condition.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">2.&#160;&#160;Risks Related to Our Affordable Housing Equity Segment</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Tax Credit Fund Partnerships</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">may not generate sufficient cash to pay amounts due to us, which may negatively impact our net income and cash flows</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Much of the revenue in our Affordable Housing Equity segment is historically earned from fees that Tax Credit Fund Partnerships we sponsor and manage pay to our subsidiaries for services rendered.&#160;&#160;These Tax Credit Fund Partnerships are dependent upon the cash flows of Tax Credit Property Partnerships in which they invest to generate their own cash flows that are used to pay such fees for services, such as asset management and advisory services.&#160;&#160;As the Tax Credit Property Partnerships are susceptible to numerous operational risks (see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">General Risks Related to Our Business &#8211; There are risks associated with investments secured by real estate, which may negatively affect our net income and cash flows</font>), the Tax Credit Fund Partnerships may not collect sufficient cash to pay the fees they owe to us.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">If we do not receive these fees, or if we determine that the amounts are not collectible, the loss of such earnings would negatively impact our net income and cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We may be unable to raise capital for new Tax Credit Fund Partnerships</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Historically, a large part of our net income is based on fees and equity income we earn for originating or managing Tax Credit Fund Partnerships, many of which have finite lives.&#160;&#160;Our current strategy to expand our third party asset management business is dependent upon our ability to attract investors to Tax Credit Fund Partnerships we originate.&#160;&#160;If we are not successful in originating Tax Credit Fund Partnerships to expand our business and to replace others as they approach the end of their life cycles, our ability to earn income and generate cash flows will decline.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Additionally, real estate underlies most of our business lines, whether by virtue of sponsoring Tax Credit Fund Partnerships associated with real estate or by direct investment.&#160;&#160;While sometimes viewed as an attractive investment sector, there is no guarantee that the investors in the Tax Credit Fund Partnerships we sponsor will continue to allocate capital to investments associated with real estate.&#160;&#160;Should there be a general decline in capital invested in the sector, our ability to sponsor Tax Credit Fund Partnerships would be diminished and the income we earn from these activities would decline.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">There is a risk of elimination of, or changes to, governmental programs that could limit our product offerings</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">A significant portion of our Affordable Housing Equity segment revenues is derived from the syndication of partnership interests in partnerships that invest in properties eligible for LIHTCs which are a provision of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#8220;Code&#8221;).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Section 42 of the Code authorizes federal LIHTCs for affordable multifamily rental housing.&#160;&#160;Under this program, a property either receives an allocation of federal LIHTCs from an agency designated by the government of the state in which the property is located or the property is entitled to the LIHTCs by reason of its being financed by volume cap mortgage revenue bonds.&#160;&#160;There are two types of credits:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">4% credits &#8211; for new buildings and existing buildings financed with mortgage revenue bonds that receive an allocation of the volume cap, or for new and existing buildings financed with below-market federal financing that receive an allocation of federal LIHTCs from state agencies; and</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">9% credits &#8211; for new or substantially rehabilitated buildings that receive an allocation of federal LIHTCs from state agencies.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The credits are typically taken over a period of ten years, which can span over an 11-year operating period.&#160;&#160;The credit amount is based on the qualified basis of each building, which is based upon the adjusted basis of the building multiplied by the percentage of units in the building leased to low-income tenants.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In order to qualify for the federal LIHTC, the property must comply with either of the &#8220;20/50&#8221; or &#8220;40/60&#8221; tests that apply to tax-exempt bonds<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>(see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">The treatment of our income as federally tax exempt depends upon the application of tax laws that could be challenged </font>under<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"> Risks Related to Application of Tax Laws</font> later in this section).&#160;&#160;In addition, the amount of rent that may be charged to qualifying low-income tenants cannot exceed 30% of the &#8220;imputed income&#8221; for each unit, i.e., 30% of the imputed income of a family earning 50% or 60% of area median income, as adjusted for family size.&#160;&#160;Failure to comply continuously with these requirements throughout the 15-year recapture period could result in a recapture of the federal LIHTCs.&#160;&#160;In addition, if the rents from the property are not sufficient to pay debt service on the mortgage revenue bonds or other financing secured by the property and a default ensues, the initial borrower could lose ownership of the project as a result of foreclosure of the mortgage.&#160;&#160;In such event, the initial equity investors would no longer be entitled to claim the federal LIHTCs, but the foreclosing lender could claim the remaining LIHTCs provided the project continues to be operated in accordance with the requirements of Section 42.&#160;&#160;As a result, there is a strong incentive for the federal LIHTC investor to ensure that the development is current on debt service payments by making additional capital contributions or otherwise.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">With respect to most of the properties, substantially all the multifamily units are rented to individuals or families earning no greater than 60% of area median income and, thus, substantially all of the qualified basis may be used to determine the amount of the federal LIHTC.&#160;&#160;This maximizes the amount of equity raised from the purchasers of the federal LIHTCs for each development and provides for the maximum amount of rent that can be obtained from tenants where there is currently strong occupancy demand.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Tax Credit Fund Partnerships we sponsor contribute the negotiated equity to the developer/owner, paid over a period of time.&#160;&#160;In the case of properties utilizing 4% credits, this contribution will usually provide between 25% and 35% of the costs of the development.&#160;&#160;For properties utilizing 9% credits, this contribution will usually provide between 45% and 55% of the cost of the development.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Since LIHTCs are a part of the Code, Congress could repeal or modify this legislation at any time or modify the tax laws so that the value of LIHTC benefits is reduced.&#160;&#160;If such legislation is repealed or adversely modified, we would no longer be able to pursue this portion of our business strategy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our role as a sponsor of Tax Credit Fund Partnerships and co-developer of Tax Credit Property Partnerships exposes us to risks of loss</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In connection with the sponsorship of Tax Credit Fund Partnerships and joint venture activities for co-development of Tax Credit Property Partnerships, we act as a fiduciary to the investors in our Tax Credit Fund Partnerships and in certain cases also provide performance guarantees to these investors.&#160;&#160;We advance funds to acquire interests in Tax Credit Property Partnerships for inclusion in Tax Credit Fund Partnerships and, at any point in time, the amount of funds advanced can be material.&#160;&#160;Recovery of these amounts is subject to our ability to attract investors to new Tax Credit Fund Partnerships or, if investors are not found, the sale of the partnership interests in the underlying properties.&#160;&#160;We could also be liable to investors in Tax Credit Fund Partnerships and third parties as a result of serving as general partner or special limited partner in various Tax Credit Fund Partnerships.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In addition, investors in the Tax Credit Fund Partnerships we sponsor and manage anticipate certain returns on their investment and for certain Tax Credit Fund Partnerships we have agreed to provide specified rates of return.&#160;&#160;If the Tax Credit Property Partnerships in which these funds invest do not perform as expected, we may be required to make payments in order to cover shortfalls at the Tax Credit Property Partnership level or to insure Tax Credit Fund Partnerships produce their specified level of return (see also<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"> There are risks associated with credit intermediation</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">and commitments to provide specified rates of return that could reduce our reported income</font>)<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">.</font></font></font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We may advance monies to a Tax Credit Fund Partnership to cover shortfalls at the Tax Credit Property Partnership level, although we are not required to do so, to maintain our relationship with Tax Credit Fund Partnership investors and to preserve the value of our residual interests in the mortgage revenue bonds we re-securitized.&#160;&#160;If we make such advances, there can be no assurance that we will be able to recover the monies.&#160;&#160;If we determine that any such advances are not recoverable, the negative impact on our net income and cash flows could be material.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">There are risks associated with credit intermediation</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">and commitments to provide specified rates of return that could reduce our reported income</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Through our subsidiaries, we have provided credit intermediation to third parties.&#160;&#160;These contracts provide for payment to cover shortfalls at properties or provide specified internal rates of return to investors in Tax Credit Fund Partnerships we sponsor.&#160;&#160;All of these credit intermediation agreements have been executed at isolated special purpose entities. These isolated special purpose entities have been capitalized to meet the payments required under these agreements, however in certain cases we may be required to make additional payments to these isolated special purpose entities if the Tax Credit Property Partnerships related to these agreements do not perform as expected.&#160;&#160;In certain instances these isolated special purpose entities are required to advance funds to a Tax Credit Fund Partnership to cover shortfalls at the Tax Credit Property Partnership level in order to insure that the investors do not lose their expected tax benefits and, if the internal rate of return to investors falls below the specified level, these subsidiaries would be required to make a payment so that the specified rate of return is achieved.&#160;&#160;If third parties default on their obligations for which these subsidiaries provided credit intermediation, our reported loss would likely be in an amount far in excess of the fee paid to us for providing the service.&#160;&#160;If advances are made to cover shortfalls at the Tax Credit Property Partnership level, there can be no assurance that we will be able to recover the monies.&#160;&#160;If we determine that any such advances are not recoverable, the negative impact on our net income and cash flows could be material. The maximum potential liability pursuant to these transactions is detailed in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 7 &#8211; Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis &#8211; SECTION 3 &#8211; Financial Condition &#8211; Commitments and Contingencies &#8211; Off Balance Sheet Arrangements</font> and Note 31 to the consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During the fourth quarter of 2010, we did not complete the restructuring of certain bonds by the date required in the Master Novation, Stabilization, Assignment, Allocation, Servicing and Asset Management Agreement with Natixis (&#8220;Natixis Master Agreement&#8221;), which resulted in a cash freeze event under the terms of that agreement.&#160;&#160;As a result of the cash freeze event, we must obtain consent from Natixis prior to any usage of available cash at CFin Holdings, one of the isolated special purpose entities described above that is required to provide intermediation services to certain of our Tax Credit Fund Partnerships.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Certain management agreements have finite terms and may not be renewed which could negatively affect our net income and cash flows</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We receive fees from Tax Credit Fund Partnerships we sponsor and manage.&#160;&#160;These Tax Credit Fund Partnerships generally do not require or authorize their investors to approve the funds&#8217; management arrangements with us as we will generally have controlling interests in the Tax Credit Fund Partnership or the entities which control the Tax Credit Fund Partnership.&#160;&#160;However, our management is subject to a fiduciary duty to the investors in those Tax Credit Fund Partnerships, which may affect our ability to continue to collect the fees and equity allocations.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, the organizational documents of certain of these Tax Credit Fund Partnerships allow for the investors to remove us as general partner or managing member without cause or upon the occurrence of certain events.&#160;&#160;Although the Tax Credit Fund Partnerships will generally be required to pay fair market value if they exercise this right, our right to receive future fees would terminate and there can be no assurance that the payment will fully compensate us for the future loss in revenue.&#160;&#160;Finally, many of these Tax Credit Fund Partnerships have finite lives, after which they are liquidated.&#160;&#160;The termination of a fund will result in a termination of the fees we receive from it.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">3.&#160;&#160;Risks Related to Our Affordable Housing Debt Segment</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">There are risks associated with our investment in Freddie Mac B-Certificates, which may negatively affect our net income and cash flows.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In addition to the above risk factor entitled <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">There are risks associated with investments secured by real estate, which may negatively affect our net income and cash flows, </font>there are additional risks associated with our investment in Freddie Mac B-Certificates.&#160;&#160;Cash received and income recorded on our Freddie Mac B-Certificates is impacted by third party support of the properties underlying this investment as well as the restructuring of non-performing property debt underlying this investment.&#160;&#160;We have entered into agreements with Merrill Lynch and Natixis Financial Products which contemplate ongoing support for certain properties as well as the restructuring of non-performing property debt.&#160;&#160;Consummation of the specific support provisions included in these agreements is dependent on various conditions being met.&#160;&#160;These conditions may not be met or these agreements may be amended or modified which may negatively impact the cash received and income recorded on our Freddie Mac B-Certificates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We also participate in loss sharing transactions for loans we originated under Freddie Mac&#8217;s DUI program whereby we have originated loans that were purchased by Freddie Mac.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of our master agreement with Freddie Mac, we are obligated to reimburse Freddie Mac for a portion of any loss that may result from borrower defaults in DUI transactions.&#160;&#160;For such loans, if a default occurs, our share of the loss will be the first 5% of the unpaid principal balance and 25% of the next 20% of the remaining unpaid principal balance to a maximum of 10% of the unpaid principal balance.&#160;&#160;The loss on a defaulted loan is calculated as the unpaid principal amount due, unpaid interest due and default resolutions costs (taxes, insurance, operation and foreclosure costs) less recoveries.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, we had 59 loss sharing loans in this program.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">If our loan servicing portfolio decreases, our net income and cash flows would be negatively affected</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">A large portion of our revenues in the mortgage origination business relate to recurring fees for servicing mortgages we originate or those for which we have sub-servicing agreements.&#160;&#160;Loans in our portfolio are subject to maturity, prepayments, defaults and refinancing after which we may not recapture the loan.&#160;&#160;Upon these events, our portfolio would decline, depriving us of the associated revenue stream.&#160;&#160;This, in turn, would negatively affect our net income and cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">4.&#160;&#160;Risks Related to Our Mortgage Banking Segment</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">There are risks of loss associated with our mortgage originations that may negatively impact our net income and cash flows</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Under the DUS program, we originate loans through one of our subsidiaries that are thereafter purchased or credit enhanced by Fannie Mae and sold to third party investors.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to a master loss sharing agreement with Fannie Mae, we retain a first loss position with respect to the loans that we originate and sell under this program.&#160;&#160;For these loss sharing loans, we assume responsibility for a portion of any loss that may result from borrower defaults, based on the Fannie Mae loss sharing formulas, and Fannie Mae risk Levels I, II or III.&#160;&#160;All of the 1,019 loss sharing loans in this program as of December 31, 2011, were Level I loans.&#160;&#160;For a majority of these loans, if a default occurs, we are responsible for the first 5% of the unpaid principal balance and a portion of any additional losses to a maximum of 20% of the original principal balance; any remaining loss is borne by Fannie Mae.&#160;&#160;A modified risk sharing arrangement is applied to 93 loans in which our risk share is reduced to 0% to 75% of our overall share of the loss.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to this agreement, we are responsible for funding 100% of mortgagor delinquency (principal and interest) and servicing advances (taxes, insurance and foreclosure costs) until the amounts advanced exceed 5% of the unpaid principal balance at the date of default.&#160;&#160;Thereafter, for Level I loans, we may request interim loss sharing adjustments which allow us to fund 25% of such advances until final settlement under the master loss sharing agreement.&#160;&#160;No interim sharing adjustments are available for Level II and Level III loans.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our maximum &#8220;first loss&#8221; exposure under the DUS and DUI programs is detailed in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 7 &#8211; Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis &#8211; SECTION 3 &#8211; Financial Condition &#8211; Commitments and Contingencies - Off Balance Sheet Arrangements</font> and Note 31 to the consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">5.&#160;&#160;Risks Related to Application of Tax Laws</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">We may not realize the value of net operating loss carry forwards</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Due to significant operating losses over the past several years, we have a significant net operating loss (&#8220;NOL&#8221;) that can be carried forward to offset taxable income in future periods.&#160;&#160;While we currently carry the deferred tax asset related to the NOL carry forward at zero value due to uncertainty of utilization in the near term, since the NOL may be carried forward for a period of 20 years, there is potential value in the deferred tax asset.&#160;&#160;Should the IRS determine that we underwent a &#8220;change of control&#8221; of more than 50%, certain provisions of the Code would substantially eliminate our ability to utilize loss carry forwards.&#160;&#160;If such an event were to occur, the cash flow benefits we might otherwise realize from utilizing the NOL carry forwards would be eliminated.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, strategies we may follow to address these risks carry risks of their own, as described in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Risks Related to Investing in Our Company &#8211; Our anti-takeover provisions may discourage third-party proposals</font>.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the companies with the tax losses are open to federal, state and local audit for the tax years 2008 &#8211; 2010.&#160;&#160;To date, we have settled federal and state audits for the tax years through 2007 without any significant negative audit adjustments. The federal and state audits for 2008 have begun and no significant negative adjustments have been proposed thus far. Should the federal, state or local tax authorities successfully reduce our tax losses claimed in these open tax years, the amount of loss carry forwards disclosed as available to offset future taxable income would be reduced.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our former classification as a publicly traded partnership not taxable as a corporation is not free from doubt and could be challenged during tax periods open for IRS examination</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Effective July 31, 2011, Centerline Holding Company (&#8220;CHC&#8221;) elected to be taxed as a corporation.&#160;&#160;Prior to that, we were taxed as a flow-through entity, which allowed us to pass-through some of our income, including our federally tax-exempt income, and deductions to our shareholders.&#160;&#160;For periods prior to the Election, the listing of our Common Shares on the Over-the-Counter Exchange caused us to be treated as a &#8220;publicly traded partnership&#8221; for federal income tax purposes.&#160;&#160;For periods prior to the Election, we believe that we were properly treated as a partnership for federal income tax purposes.&#160;&#160;However, for periods prior to the Election, the Internal Revenue Service (&#8220;IRS&#8221;) could challenge our partnership status and we could fail to qualify as a partnership in years that are subject to audit.&#160;&#160;Qualification as a partnership involves the application of numerous technical legal provisions.&#160;&#160;For example, a publicly traded partnership is generally taxable as a corporation unless 90% or more of its gross income is &#8220;qualifying&#8221; income (which includes interest, dividends, real property rents, gains from the sale or other disposition of real property, gain from the sale or other disposition of capital assets held for the production of interest or dividends, and certain other items).&#160;&#160;We have represented that in all prior years of our existence and for the period up to the Election, at least 90% of our gross income was qualifying income.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In determining whether interest is treated as qualifying income under these rules, interest income derived from a &#8220;financial business&#8221; and income and gains derived by a &#8220;dealer&#8221; in securities are not treated as qualifying income.&#160;&#160;For periods prior to the Election, we have represented that we were acting as an investor with respect to our remaining mortgage revenue bond investments and that we have not engaged in a financial business, although there is no clear guidance on what constitutes a financial business under the tax law.&#160;&#160;For periods prior to the Election, we have taken the position that for purposes of determining whether we are in a financial business, Affordable Housing Equity activities would not cause us to be engaged in a financial business or to be considered a &#8220;dealer&#8221; in securities.&#160;&#160;The IRS could assert that our activities constituted a financial business.&#160;&#160;If our activities constituted a financial business or cause us to be treated as a dealer, there is a substantial risk that more than 10% of our gross income would not constitute qualifying income.&#160;&#160;We could also be treated as if we were engaged in a financial business if the activities of Centerline Capital Group&#160;LLC (&#8220;CCG&#8221;) and its subsidiaries were attributed to us and were determined to constitute a financial business.&#160;&#160;CCG is subject to income tax on its income.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, for periods prior to the Election, we believe the activities and income of CCG and its subsidiaries will not be attributed to CHC for purposes of determining the Company&#8217;s tax status.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For periods prior to the Election if, for any reason, less than 90% of our gross income constituted qualifying income, items of income and deduction would not pass-through to our shareholders and our shareholders would be treated for federal income tax purposes as stockholders in a corporation.&#160;&#160;We would be required to pay income tax at corporate rates on any portion of our net income that did not constitute tax-exempt income.&#160;&#160;In addition, a portion of our federally tax-exempt income may be included in determining our alternative minimum tax liability.&#160;&#160;Distributions by us to our shareholders would constitute dividend income taxable to such holders to the extent of our earnings and profits, which would include tax-exempt income, as well as any taxable income we might have, and the payment of these distributions would not be deductible by us.&#160;&#160;For periods prior to the Election, these consequences could have a material adverse effect on us, our shareholders and consequently, the current price of our shares.&#160;&#160;For periods after the Election, we have determined that being taxable as a corporation would not result in significant additional tax liabilities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">There is a risk that the IRS will disagree with our judgment with respect to allocations</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Effective July 31, 2011, CHC elected to be taxed as a corporation. For periods prior to the Election, we used various accounting and reporting conventions to determine each shareholder&#8217;s allocable share of income, including any market discount taxable as ordinary income, gain, loss and deductions.&#160;&#160;Our allocation provisions will be respected for federal income tax purposes only if they are considered to have &#8220;substantial economic effect&#8221; or are in accordance with the partners&#8217; &#8220;interest in the partnership&#8221;.&#160;&#160;There is no assurance that the IRS will agree with our various accounting methods, conventions and allocation provisions, particularly our allocation of adjustments to shareholders attributable to the differences between the shareholders&#8217; purchase price of Common Shares and their shares of our tax basis in our assets, pursuant to an election we made.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">The structure of our acquisitions could be challenged</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Effective July 31, 2011, CHC elected to be taxed as a corporation.&#160;&#160;Our acquisitions of Centerline Affordable Housing Advisors LLC (&#8220;CAHA&#8221;) and other subsidiaries were structured to prevent us from realizing active income from these businesses for periods prior to the Election and to effectively receive a tax deduction (via the allocation of subsidiary income) for payments made to its selling principals.&#160;&#160;It is possible that the IRS could challenge this structure, with material adverse consequences to us for periods prior to the Election.&#160;&#160;First, the IRS could assert that we, as the parent trust, are the owner of these businesses, in which case the parent trust would realize an amount of active income from them that would require it to be treated as a corporation instead of a partnership for income tax purposes.&#160;&#160;If the IRS prevailed, that income would be includable in taxable income or loss for periods prior to the Election.&#160;&#160;Even though the Company has currently suspended its distributions, it is still possible that if the IRS prevailed, the value of our shares would decline.&#160;&#160;Second, the IRS might assert that the Special Common Units (&#8220;SCUs&#8221;) held by the selling principals of the businesses and others are actually shares of our Company.&#160;&#160;If this position prevailed, the distributions payable on the units would not reduce the taxable income of CCG.&#160;&#160;In such event, CCG would be subject to increased tax, which could reduce our net income, our cash flows and our distributions, which could also result in a decrease in the portion of our distributions that is excluded from gross income for federal income tax purposes for periods prior to the Election.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The treatment of our income as federally tax exempt depends upon the application of tax laws that could be challenged</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In our Affordable Housing Equity segment, we invest primarily in investments that generate tax-exempt income.&#160;&#160;However, the IRS may seek to re-characterize a portion of our tax-exempt income as taxable income as described in the <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Tax-exemption of interest on mortgage revenue bonds</font> section below.&#160;&#160;If the IRS were successful, for the periods prior to the Election, a shareholder&#8217;s distributive share of such income would be taxable to the shareholder, regardless of whether an amount of cash equal to such distributive share is actually distributed.&#160;&#160;Any taxable income would be allocated pro rata among our Convertible CRA Shares and our Common Shares.&#160;&#160;The Company has suspended its distributions, and as a result, the Convertible CRA Shares are not currently allocated any income.&#160;&#160;For the periods after the Election, the income would be taxable to the Company.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Tax-exemption of interest on mortgage revenue bonds</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">On the date of original issuance or re-issuance of each mortgage revenue bond, nationally recognized bond counsel or special tax counsel rendered its opinion to the effect that, based on the law in effect on that date, interest on such mortgage revenue bonds is excludable from federally-taxable gross income, except with respect to any revenue bond&#160;&#160;during any period in which it is held by a &#8220;substantial user&#8221; of the property financed with the proceeds of such mortgage revenue bonds or a &#8220;related person&#8221; of such a &#8220;substantial user.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Each opinion speaks only as of the date it was delivered.&#160;&#160;However, an opinion of counsel has no binding effect and there is no assurance that the IRS will not contest these conclusions or, if contested, that they will be sustained by a court.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Code establishes certain requirements which must be met subsequent to the issuance and delivery of tax-exempt mortgage revenue bonds for interest on such mortgage revenue bonds to remain excludable from federally-taxable gross income.&#160;&#160;Among these continuing requirements are restrictions on the investment and use of the revenue bond proceeds.&#160;&#160;In addition, there is a requirement that the property be operated as a rental property and that during the Qualified Project Period (defined below) at least either:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
