<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">G.&#160;&#160;Investments &#8211; Other Accounting Methodologies</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Other investments consist of the following:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Mortgage Loans Held for Sale </font>&#8211; Mortgage loans held for sale represent amounts due for mortgage loans sold under purchase agreements to permanent investors, but for which we are awaiting settlement of funds.&#160;&#160;We do not retain any interest in these loans except for mortgage servicing rights (&#8220;MSRs&#8221;) and certain contingent liabilities pursuant to loss sharing agreements.&#160;&#160;We account for mortgage loans held for sale at the lower of cost or fair value.&#160;&#160;As we originate loans for sale only when we have a firm sale commitment for the principal amount of the loan, the carrying value generally represents their respective principal balances.&#160;&#160;The cost of the loans includes deferred loan commitment fee revenue net of direct costs associated with closing the related loan and we recognize these amounts in operations when the loans are sold.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Stabilization Escrow </font>&#8211; As part of the December 2007 re-securitization, certain cash consideration was placed into escrow in connection with mortgage revenue bonds for which the underlying property was not considered stabilized.&#160;&#160;As these properties stabilize, subject to certain conditions, we are able to recoup amounts from escrow.&#160;&#160;We record deposits to the stabilization escrow at the net present value of the amount deposited, taking into account the timing of releases from escrow, expected income to be earned on the cash balance and an appropriate discount rate reflecting the risk of property stabilization.&#160;&#160;We record income from the stabilization escrow (including accretion of the discount recorded upon deposit) using the effective yield method.&#160;&#160;Following the write-down of the asset (see Note 10), we record interest income based on cash receipts.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Mortgage Loans Held for Investment &#8211;</font>Mortgage loans held for investment are carried at amortized cost.&#160;&#160;We periodically evaluate our portfolio of mortgage loans for loan loss.&#160;&#160;When full collection is not expected, we record a specific valuation allowance to write the loan down to its realizable value.&#160;&#160;We measure the realizable value of an impaired loan based on:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 54pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#8217;s effective interest rate;</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 54pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">the loan&#8217;s observable market price; or</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">the fair value of the collateral if the loan is collateral-dependent.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Market prices are determined by using a combination of updated appraised values and broker quotes or services supplying market and sales data in various geographical locations where the collateral is located.&#160;&#160;If a loan is considered impaired, we also review other loans in the portfolio with similar risk characteristics and record a general valuation allowance if necessary.&#160;&#160;Valuation allowances are included in &#8220;Loss on impairment of assets&#8221; in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For more information regarding other investments see Note 10.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">H.&#160;&#160;Intangible Assets, net</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We do not amortize intangible assets with indefinite lives (such as mortgage banking licenses) but we amortize other intangible assets on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">I.&#160;&#160;Mortgage Servicing Rights, net</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We recognize as assets the rights to service mortgage loans for others, whether the MSRs are acquired through a separate purchase or through loans we originate and sell.&#160;&#160;We record purchased MSRs at cost, which approximates fair value.&#160;&#160;For originated loans, we allocate total proceeds from the sale of the loan (including the fair value of the MSR retained) and recognize a gain.&#160;&#160;Management values the MSRs based on various inputs, including information from third-party valuation specialists.&#160;&#160;The inputs include contractual servicing fees, our projected cost to service as well as estimates of default rates, prepayment speeds and an appropriate discount rate.&#160;&#160;While certain of the inputs such as fee rates and discount rates are observable, most of the other inputs are based on historical company data.&#160;&#160;In subsequent periods, we carry the assets at the amortized initial basis.&#160;&#160;We amortize all MSRs in proportion to, and over the period of, estimated net servicing income.&#160;&#160;Significant judgment is required in accounting for these assets, including:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CENTERLINE HOLDING COMPANY</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We assess our MSRs for impairment based on the fair value of the assets as compared to carrying values.&#160;&#160;We estimate the fair value by obtaining market information with the assistance of third-party valuation specialists.&#160;&#160;To determine impairment, the mortgage servicing portfolio is stratified by the risk characteristics of the underlying mortgage loans and we compare the estimated fair value of each stratum to its carrying value.&#160;&#160;With respect to our primary servicing portfolio, we have determined that the predominant risk characteristics are the interest rate and type of loan.&#160;&#160;For our other servicing portfolios we have determined that the predominant risk characteristic is the ability to generate a consistent income stream per loan due to the short-term nature of the loans being serviced or due to the fact that certain servicing revenues are non-recurring.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">When the carrying value of MSRs exceeds fair value, we recognize impairment charges through earnings; fair value in excess of the amount capitalized is not recognized.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For more information regarding MSRs, see Note 12.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">J.&#160;&#160;Deferred Costs and Other Assets, net</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Deferred Costs &#8211; </font>We capitalize costs incurred in connection with issuance of debt and mandatorily redeemable equity issued by our subsidiaries and amortize them on a straight-line basis over the terms of the facilities, or in the case of Equity Issuer over the period to the expected repurchase date of the shares (which approximates the effective interest method).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Land, Property and Buildings </font>&#8211;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>Our Consolidated Partnerships segment includes Tax Credit Property Partnerships with multifamily apartment properties and other properties upon which the funds have foreclosed.&#160;&#160;The property assets are depreciated over 7 to 40 year periods.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Furniture, Fixtures and Leasehold Improvements, net</font> &#8211; Furniture, fixtures and leasehold improvements are stated at cost.&#160;&#160;Depreciation is calculated using the straight-line method over their estimated useful lives.&#160;&#160;Leasehold improvements are amortized using the straight-line method over the shorter of their useful lives or the life of the lease.&#160;&#160;Costs associated with repairs and maintenance of property are expensed as incurred.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Deferred Revenues</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In connection with our Affordable Housing Equity tax credit fund origination and management businesses, we receive revenues at the time a fund closes associated with origination, property acquisitions, partnership management services and credit intermediation.&#160;&#160;These fees are deferred and recognized over various periods as described in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">T. Revenues</font> below.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">L.&#160;&#160;Impairment of Long-lived Assets</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We review property, equipment, and other long-lived assets for impairment on an annual basis and whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amounts of such assets may not be recoverable. If such events or changes in circumstances occur, we will recognize an impairment loss if the undiscounted future cash flows expected to be generated by the asset are less than the carrying value of the related asset. The impairment loss would adjust the asset to its fair value, which would become its new cost basis.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">M.&#160;&#160;Shares of Subsidiaries</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The effects of any changes in our ownership interests resulting from the issuance of equity capital by consolidated subsidiaries or equity investees to unaffiliated parties are accounted for as capital transactions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Equity Issuer has issued multiple series of Cumulative Preferred Shares, some of which are subject to mandatory repurchase, and others which are not. We classify the Cumulative Preferred Shares subject to mandatory purchase as liabilities on our Consolidated Balance Sheets and include the dividends paid for those share as interest expense in our Consolidated Statements of Operations.&#160;&#160;For those shares not subject to mandatory repurchase, we classify them as non-controlling interests within equity in our Consolidated Balance Sheets and the associated dividends are included in &#8220;Net loss attributed to non-controlling interests&#8221; in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CENTERLINE HOLDING COMPANY</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">N.&#160;&#160;Securitization Activities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We have engaged in securitization activities related to financial assets including mortgage revenue bonds.&#160;&#160;The exposure to credit losses from securitized assets is limited to our retained interest, including any credit intermediation we may provide through our Affordable Housing Equity segment.&#160;&#160;Retained interests, which currently include certain Freddie Mac Certificates held by our Affordable Housing Debt segment, are accounted for in accordance with the nature and terms of the retained interests (see also <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">E. Investments &#8211; Available-for-Sale </font>above).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For more information see Notes 8, 16 and 31.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">O.&#160;&#160;Resale and Repurchase Agreements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We account for transactions involving sales of securities and mortgage loans under agreements to repurchase (&#8220;repurchase agreements&#8221; or &#8220;repos&#8221;) as collateralized financing arrangements / agreements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">P.&#160;&#160;Allowance for Risk-Sharing Obligations</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We account for exposure to loss under our servicing contracts with Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac as guarantees through an allowance for risk-sharing obligations.&#160;&#160;The exposure to loss results from guarantees made to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac under the Designated Underwriting and Servicing (&#8220;DUS&#8221;) and Delegated Underwriting Initiative (&#8220;DUI&#8221;) programs to share the risk of loan losses (See Note 31 for more details).&#160;&#160;The allowance recorded is considered the fair value of the guarantees.&#160;&#160;Our determination of the adequacy of the allowance for risk-sharing obligations on loans serviced is based on an evaluation of the risk characteristics and exposure to loss associated with those loans.&#160;&#160;Our assessment is based on a number of factors including, but not limited to, general economic conditions, inability of the borrower to meet debt service requirements, a substantial decline in the value of the collateral or the risk of refinancing the loan at maturity.&#160;&#160;For performing loans, we maintain a general reserve, which is based on the stratification of the loan servicing portfolio by debt service coverage ratio (&#8220;DSCR&#8221;) and loan-to-value ratio (&#8220;LTV&#8221;) calculated from the most current net operating income (&#8220;NOI&#8221;) of the underlying properties.&#160;&#160;The probability of default and loss severity is higher for loans with lower DSCRs and poor LTV and therefore a higher reserve is maintained for such loans.&#160;&#160;For defaulted loans, we maintain a loan specific reserve based on an estimate of our share of the loss.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Q.&#160;&#160;Credit Intermediation</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Transactions</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For guarantees and other credit intermediation transactions, we record liabilities (included in deferred revenues) equal to the fair values of the obligations undertaken.&#160;&#160;For transactions for which we receive fees, we consider the fees received to be fair value.&#160;&#160;For completion and other guarantees issued to lenders for the underlying financing of properties, as required by an investment fund, we generally recognize no liability upon inception of the guarantee as the exposure is considered minimal and no fee is received.&#160;&#160;We monitor our exposure under these agreements and, should we determine a loss is probable, accrue a liability for the estimated loss.&#160;&#160;For more information, see Note 31.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">R.&#160;&#160;Financial Risk Management and Derivatives</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our primary objective for holding derivative instruments is to manage interest rate risks.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our derivative instruments are comprised of free-standing derivatives.&#160;&#160;We carry derivative instruments at their estimated fair values on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;We include all changes in fair value as well as the impact of terminations within interest expense in our Consolidated Statements of Operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The fair values of interest rate swaps are determined using the market standard methodology of netting the discounted future fixed cash receipts (or payments) and the discounted expected variable cash payments (or receipts).&#160;&#160;The variable cash payments (or receipts) are based on an expectation of future interest rates (forward curve) derived from observable market interest rate curves.&#160;&#160;In adjusting the fair value of our derivative contracts for the effect of nonperformance risk, we have considered the impact of netting and any applicable credit enhancements, such as thresholds and guarantees.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">S.&#160;&#160;Treasury Stock</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We account for treasury stock purchases using the cost method.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">T.&#160;&#160;Revenues</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Interest Income</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Significant components of interest income include:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Mortgage revenue bond interest income </font>&#8211; We recognize mortgage revenue bond interest income using the effective yield method based on the actual coupon rate and the outstanding principal amount of the underlying mortgages, taking into account differences in interest rate during the construction period as compared to balance of the term, premiums and discounts, any fees received in connection with bond originations and the effects of estimated prepayments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Other interest income </font>&#8211; We recognize income on temporary investments (such as cash in banks and short-term instruments) as well as longer term investments (e.g., promissory notes, mortgages receivable) and escrow accounts we manage, on the accrual basis as earned.&#160;&#160;We recognize income on retained interest certificates (including the Freddie Mac certificates) as it accrues, provided collectability of future amounts is reasonably assured.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We place investments on a non-accrual status when any portion of the principal or interest is 90 days past due or earlier when concern exists as to the ultimate collectability of principal or interest.&#160;&#160;Investments return to accrual status when principal and interest become current.&#160;&#160;There were 19 investments on non-accrual status at December 31, 2011, and 25 at December 31 2010, with a fair value of $43.2 million and $122.0 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;Amounts collected while on non-accrual status are applied as a reduction of the related principal balance.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Fee Income</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Fees related to our Affordable Housing Equity segment&#8217;s Tax Credit Fund Partnerships sponsorship activities, associated with sponsoring Tax Credit Fund Partnerships and for assisting the funds in acquiring assets include:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CENTERLINE HOLDING COMPANY</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Servicing fees</font> related to mortgages are recognized on an accrual basis as the services are performed over the servicing period by our Mortgage Banking and Affordable Housing Debt segment.&#160;&#160;These fees are generally based on a percentage of the balance of loans serviced, and we record them as earned on an accrual basis provided that collection is reasonably assured.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Credit intermediation fees</font>, earned by our Affordable Housing Equity segment, are for transactions to provide specified rates of return for a tax credit fund.&#160;&#160;These fees are received in advance, are deferred and amortized over the applicable risk-weighted periods on a straight-line basis.&#160;&#160;For those pertaining to the construction and lease-up phase of a pool of properties, the periods are generally one to five years.&#160;&#160;For those pertaining to the operational phase of a pool of properties, the period is approximately 20 years.&#160;&#160;Fees for other credit intermediation transactions are received monthly and recognized as income when earned.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Other Revenues</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We recognize gains upon the sale of mortgage loans if the sale price exceeds the carrying value and in connection with recording MSRs (see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">I. Mortgage Servicing Rights, Net </font>above).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Other revenues also include prepayment penalties recognized at the time of prepayment of an investment and expense reimbursements for amounts billed to investment funds and other affiliated entities for reimbursement of salaries and certain other ongoing operating expenditures, which we recognize as earned based on collectability.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Rental Income</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Rental income for Tax Credit Property Partnerships is accrued as earned based on underlying lease agreements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">U.&#160;&#160;Share-Based Compensation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We record restricted share grants in beneficial owners&#8217; equity.&#160;&#160;The balance recorded equals the number of shares issued (and that we expect to vest) multiplied by the closing price of our Common Shares on the grant date.&#160;&#160;We recognize the value of the awards as expense in our Consolidated Statements of Operations on a straight-line basis over the applicable service periods.&#160;&#160;For each separately vesting portion of an award, we record the expense as if the award was, in substance, multiple awards.&#160;&#160;We expense any shares granted with immediate vesting when granted.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Because share-based compensation is based on awards that we ultimately expect to vest, share-based compensation expense has been reduced to account for estimated forfeitures.&#160;&#160;We estimate forfeitures at the time of grant and revise the estimate, if necessary, in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For share option grants, we are required to select a valuation technique or option pricing model that meets the criteria as stated in ASC 718, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Compensation &#8211; Stock Compensation</font>.&#160;&#160;We use the Black-Scholes model, which requires the input of subjective assumptions.&#160;&#160;These assumptions include estimating the length of time employees will retain their vested stock options before exercising them (&#8220;expected term&#8221;), the estimated volatility of the Company&#8217;s common stock price over the expected term (&#8220;volatility&#8221;), the risk free interest rate and the dividend yield.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For more information see Note 25.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">V.&#160;&#160;Income Taxes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We recognize deferred tax assets and liabilities for the expected future tax consequences of temporary differences between the financial statement carrying amounts and the tax basis of assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;We assess the recoverability of deferred tax assets through evaluation of carryback availability, projected taxable income and other factors as applicable.&#160;&#160;If we determine that deferred tax assets may not be recoverable, we record a valuation allowance as appropriate.&#160;&#160;Significant judgment is required in assessing the future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in our consolidated financial statements or tax returns as well as the recoverability of amounts we record, including deferred tax assets.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, these projected future tax consequences include our assumption as to the continuing tax-exempt nature of a portion of our earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We provide for exposure in connection with uncertain tax positions which requires significant judgment by management including determination, based on the weight of the tax law and available evidence, that it is more-likely-than-not that a tax result will be realized.&#160;&#160;Our policy is to recognize interest and/or penalties related to income tax matters in income tax expense on our Consolidated Statements of Operations.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, we accrued no interest and no penalties related to <a name="jump_exp_1"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>uncertain <a name="jump_exp_2"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>tax <a name="jump_exp_3"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>positions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For more information see Note 26.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">W.&#160;&#160;Earnings per Share</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We utilize the two-class method of calculating earnings per share (&#8220;EPS&#8221;), as redeemable shares (see Note 19) and unvested share grants (see Note 25) contractually entitle their holders to participate in dividends and earnings of the Company (rendering them &#8220;Participating Securities&#8221;). Accordingly, we allocate available earnings between the Common and Participating Security shareholders.&#160;&#160;For purposes of the calculation, available earnings represent net income or loss attributable to the Company&#8217;s shareholders after deduction of:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Weighted average shares outstanding include Common Shares and Series A Convertible Community Reinvestment Act Preferred Shares (&#8220;Convertible CRA Shares&#8221;) that are not redeemable as they have the same economic benefits as the Common Shares.&#160;&#160;Basic EPS is then calculated by dividing the available earnings allocated to Common Shareholders by the weighted average number of shares outstanding.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Diluted EPS is calculated using the weighted average number of shares outstanding during the period plus the dilutive effect of potential future issuances of common stock relating to stock compensation programs and other potentially dilutive securities using the treasury stock method.&#160;&#160;Convertible redeemable shares and our subsidiaries&#8217; convertible equity units are not included in the calculation as their assumed conversions would be anti-dilutive for the periods presented.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We present basic EPS for common stock; the diluted EPS amounts pertain to our Common Shares and non-redeemable, Convertible CRA Shares.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">X.&#160;&#160;Recently Issued and Adopted Accounting Standards</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During 2011 we adopted the following new accounting pronouncements:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>

<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In January 2011, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) 2011-01, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Receivables (Topic 310):</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Deferral of the Effective Date of Disclosures about </font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Troubled Debt Restructurings in Update No. 2010-20.&#160;&#160;</font>The amendments temporarily delay the effective date of the disclosures about troubled debt restructurings in ASU 2010-20 for public entities.&#160;&#160;Under the existing effective date in ASU 2010-20, public-entity creditors would have provided disclosures about troubled debt restructurings for periods beginning on or after December 15, 2010.&#160;&#160;The amendments in this update temporarily defer that effective date, enabling public-entity creditors to provide those disclosures after the FASB clarifies the guidance for determining what constitutes a troubled debt restructuring.&#160;&#160;This update will result in more consistent disclosures about troubled debt restructurings.&#160;&#160;This amendment does not defer the effective date of the other disclosure requirements in ASU 2010-20.&#160;&#160;ASU 2011-01 is effective upon issuance.&#160;&#160;The adoption of ASU 2010-20 and ASU 2011-01 did not have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In April 2011<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">, </font>the FASB issued ASU 2011-02, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Receivables (Topic 310): A Creditor&#8217;s Determination of Whether a Restructuring Is a Troubled Debt Restructuring.</font>&#160;&#160;The update clarifies which loan modifications constitute troubled debt restructurings and is intended to assist creditors in determining whether a modification of the terms of a receivable meets the criteria to be considered a troubled debt restructuring, both for purposes of recording an impairment loss and for disclosure of troubled debt restructurings.&#160;&#160;The update is effective for interim and annual periods beginning on or after June 15, 2011, and applies retrospectively to restructurings occurring on or after the beginning of the fiscal year of adoption for public companies.&#160;&#160;The adoption of ASU 2011-02 did not have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

This update requires companies to disclose information about financial instruments that have been offset and related arrangements to enable users of its financial statements to understand the effect of those arrangements on its financial position. Companies will be required to provide both net (offset amounts) and gross information in the notes to the financial statements for relevant assets and liabilities that are offset. <div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Restructured various components of our equity and issued a new series of shares. On March 5, 2010 the Board approved a resolution creating a series of shares of beneficial interest in the Company designated as Special Series A Shares.&#160;&#160;The Board authorized a total amount of 19.9 million of Special Series A Shares. Each Special Series A Share was equivalent to 15 Common Shares on an as-converted basis (the &#8220;Conversion Ratio&#8221;) as to both voting and economic rights.&#160;&#160;Special Series A shareholders were entitled to distributions at the same time as, and only if, we paid distributions to our Common Shareholders.&#160;&#160;Special Series A shareholders were also entitled to the same allocation of earnings as allocated to Common Shares and were not entitled to any liquidation preference.&#160;&#160;Such distributions and allocations to Special Series A shareholders would be equivalent to that of the Common Shareholders multiplied by the Conversion Ratio. In connection with the March 2010 Restructuring, we issued a total of 19.3 million Special Series A Shares.&#160;&#160;At that time, substantially all of the Convertible CRA Shares were converted into 14.0 million of Special Series A Shares.&#160;&#160;At the time of the conversion, dividends in arrears of $25.0 million for the Convertible CRA Shares were eliminated.&#160;&#160;In addition, upon conversion, we recorded an increase to Common Shareholder&#8217;s equity of $286.2 million, representing the difference between the carrying value of the Redeemable Securities at conversion and the fair value of the Special Series A Shares issued.&#160;&#160;In connection with the March 2010 Restructuring, C-III purchased 4.1 million of these shares for total proceeds of $10.0 million.&#160;&#160;In connection with the restructuring of our credit intermediation agreements, we issued 1.2 million Special Series A Shares to Natixis. Special Series A Shares were recorded to equity at fair value as of the date of issuance.&#160;&#160;On October 6, 2010, our shareholders approved the proposed amendment to our trust agreement that, among other things, increased the number of our shares authorized for issuance from 160,000,000 shares to 800,000,000 shares.&#160;&#160;At that time, all of the Special Series A shares automatically were converted at 1:15 ratio to 289,879,185 Common Shares, and;</font></div>

We also settled a $27.7 million liability (for $4.4 million in cash) with respect to a portion of transaction costs payable and related accrued interest payable in connection with the December 2007 re-securitization.&#160;&#160;As a result of the settlement, we recognized a gain on settlement of liability of $23.3 million in the first quarter of 2010.&#160;&#160;We also settled a $2.3 million liability with another vendor associated with the office space to which one of the lease terminations related, resulting in an additional $2.0 million gain on settlement of liability that we recorded in the first quarter of 2010.</font></div>

<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As part of the March 2010 Restructuring, we received total proceeds of $110.0 million of which $10.0 million was attributed to the sale of 4.1 million shares of Special Series A shares to C-III.&#160;&#160;The total proceeds attributable to the sale of assets were $100.0 million including the $60.0 million of our senior secured debt obligations that were due under our Term Loan and Revolving Credit Facility and term loan agreement and that were assumed by C-III.&#160;&#160;Cash proceeds attributable to the assets and interests disposed of amounted to $37.8 million after taking into consideration $2.2 million of working capital at the sold entities, but before amounts paid by the purchaser relating to certain assumed liabilities.&#160;&#160;Cash proceeds were used to fund $10.0 million placed in escrow, settle liabilities with unsecured creditors and pay closing costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In 2011, we raised $142.2 million of gross equity in new Affordable Housing Equity Tax Credit Fund Partnerships and continue to actively pursue new opportunities that will generate additional liquidity in the form of fee income for us.&#160;&#160;With the closing of the new Tax Credit Fund Partnerships, we received $7.6 million in fees, which improved our cash flow and liquidity.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We use asset-backed warehouse facilities to fund mortgage originations in our Mortgage Banking and Affordable Housing Debt segments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">On November 2, 2010, Fannie Mae issued changes to the DUS Capital Standards that became effective January 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;Among other provisions, the revised DUS Capital Standards raised the Restricted Liquidity Requirement by 25 basis points on Tier 2 mortgage loans and is being phased-in quarterly through the first quarter of 2014.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s implementation of the revised DUS Capital Standards through the first quarter of 2014 would increase the collateral required for our existing DUS portfolio by approximately $8.3 million assuming the full 25 basis point increase in the collateral requirement was applied to our current portfolio balance.&#160;&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2011, the collateral required for our DUS portfolio increased by $1.3 million.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, we are in compliance with the collateral requirement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In June 2011, CFin Holdings repaid, using its own cash, $20.0 million in principal amount of the CFin Holdings Credit Agreement.&#160;&#160;At that time the credit facility commitments were terminated and accrued and capitalized interest of $2.6 million was waived, resulting in a gain on settlement of liabilities in the amount of $2.6 million for the twelve months ended December 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In an effort to lower overhead expenses and improve our cash flow from operations, in August 2011, we entered into a lease modification and partial surrender agreement (&#8220;Surrender Agreement&#8221;) relating to our previous headquarters located at 625 Madison Avenue in New York.&#160;&#160;We simultaneously entered into a 15 year agreement to lease office space at 100 Church Street (&#8220;100 Church Street Lease&#8221;) which effective February 2012 is used as our New York headquarters.&#160;&#160;Except for the space that we are subletting, we ceased use of the space at 625 Madison Avenue in February 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In connection with the Surrender Agreement, we anticipate a total cash savings of approximately $11 million through December 2017 which is when the original lease for space at 625 Madison Avenue would have expired.&#160;&#160;This savings includes base rent savings, lower operating costs for the new space, and municipal tax incentives, net of estimated moving costs, brokerage fees, capital improvements, and other surrender costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As of December 31, 2011, we had 320,291 Convertible CRA Shares outstanding.&#160;&#160;As we had not repurchased these Convertible CRA Shares as of January 1, 2012, the holders of the Convertible CRA Shares have the option to require us to purchase the Convertible CRA Shares for the original gross issuance price per share (plus accumulated and unpaid distributions), which totaled approximately $6.0 million as of December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Due to the terms of the Credit Agreement, we are restricted from meeting this requirement.&#160;&#160;We are exploring with the shareholders various ways to mitigate the above-referenced repurchase risk (see also Note 32).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font size="3"><br>
</font>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CENTERLINE HOLDING COMPANY</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Note5"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>NOTE 5 &#8211; Fair Value Disclosures</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">A.&#160;&#160;General</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We have categorized our assets and liabilities recorded at fair value based upon the fair value hierarchy specified by ASC 820, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures</font> (&#8220;ASC 820&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The levels of fair value hierarchy are as follows:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Level 1 inputs utilize quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that we have the ability to access.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Level 2 inputs utilize other-than-quoted prices that are observable, either directly or indirectly.&#160;&#160;Level 2 inputs include quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, and inputs such as interest rates and yield curves that are observable at commonly quoted intervals.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Level 3 inputs are unobservable and are typically based on our own assumptions, including situations where there is little, if any, market activity.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In certain cases, the inputs used to measure fair value may fall into different levels of the fair value hierarchy.&#160;&#160;In such cases, we categorize such financial asset or liability based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement in its entirety.&#160;&#160;Our assessment of the significance of a particular input to the fair value measurement in its entirety requires judgment and considers factors specific to the asset or liability that a market participant would use.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Both observable and unobservable inputs may be used to determine the fair value of positions that are classified within the Level 3 category.&#160;&#160;As a result, the unrealized gains and losses for assets within the Level 3 category presented in the tables below may include changes in fair value that were attributable to both observable (e.g., changes in market interest rates) and unobservable (e.g., changes in historical company data) inputs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">B.&#160;&#160;Financial Assets and Liabilities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Certain assets are &#8220;marked to market&#8221; every reporting period (i.e., on a recurring basis) in accordance with GAAP.&#160;&#160;Other assets are carried at amortized cost (such as mortgage loans held for investment), are initially recorded at fair value and amortized (such as MSRs) or are carried at the lower of cost or fair value (mortgage loans held for sale); these are tested for impairment periodically and would be adjusted to fair value if impaired (i.e., measured on a non-recurring basis).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: -18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">(2)&#160;&#160; </font>A portion of the Series B Certificates relates to re-securitized mortgage revenue bonds that were not reflected as sold.&#160;Accordingly, that portion is eliminated in consolidation.&#160;The change from December 31, 2010 primarily resulted from fluctuations due to changes in the fair value of the asset.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During the years ended December 31, 2011 and 2010, we received $27.4 million and $28.2 million, respectively, in interest from the Series B Freddie Mac Certificates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Delinquent collateral loans underlying the certificates had an unpaid principal balance of $120.2 million and $190.0 million at December 31, 2011 and 2010, respectively; projected remaining losses are estimated at 3.55% or $90.1 million of the underlying securitization.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2011, there were no actual losses in the underlying securitization.&#160;&#160;Due to projections of declining cash flows (including the projected impact of a restructuring of the underlying mortgage revenue bonds as discussed in Note 24), we recorded OTTI of $78.0 million on these investments in 2010.&#160;&#160;No impairments were recorded on these investments in 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During 2010, three of the underlying properties pertaining to five bonds that were in foreclosure were sold to third parties at a loss.&#160;&#160;One of the bonds was included in the stabilized escrow pool.&#160;&#160;In order to fully pay down the bond&#8217;s outstanding principal, plus accrued interest, to the Series A-1 Freddie Mac Certificates as required per the securitization agreements, a release of $4.4 million was made from the stabilization escrow.&#160;&#160;A loss of $7.8 million for the other two mortgage revenue bonds was absorbed by the principal of the Series B Freddie Mac Certificates.&#160;&#160;There was no such loss during 2011.</font></div>

<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">A.</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Mortgage Loans Held for Sale</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Mortgage loans held for sale include originated loans either pre-sold to Government Sponsored Enterprises (&#8220;GSEs&#8221;), such as Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac or to the Government National Mortgage Association (&#8220;Ginnie Mae&#8221;) under contractual sale obligations that normally settle within 30 days of origination.&#160;&#160;In many cases, the loans sold to GSEs are used as collateral for mortgage-backed securities issued and guaranteed by GSEs and traded in the open market.&#160;&#160;Mortgage loans held for sale can differ widely from period to period depending on the timing and size of originated mortgages and variances in holding periods prior to sale.&#160;&#160;Loans closed and funded during 2011 were $1.4 billion.&#160;&#160;Loans sold and settled during 2011 were $1.3 billion.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">B.&#160;&#160;Goodwill Impairment</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In the fourth quarter of 2010, as a result of our annual goodwill impairment assessment, we determined that the remainder of the goodwill associated with our affordable housing business was impaired.&#160;&#160;This resulted in a $93.3 million impairment charge attributed to our acquisition of CAHA.&#160;&#160;The impairment was principally due to our lack of origination of LIHTC equity during 2010, which caused us to make downward revisions to our forecasted cash flows and expected returns from the operation of the affordable housing business.&#160;&#160;Both these factors resulted in a decline in enterprise value and an impairment of goodwill.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, goodwill associated with our acquisition of CAHA has been fully impaired.</font></div>
