<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CENTERLINE HOLDING COMPANY</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Note14"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>NOTE 14 &#8211; Consolidated Partnerships</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Company, through its Affordable Housing Equity segment, originates and manages Tax Credit Fund Partnerships.&#160;&#160;The Company, through one of its affiliates, controls SLP interests in each of the Tax Credit Property Partnerships acquired by the Tax Credit Fund Partnerships.&#160;&#160;In our role as SLP, we are able to remove the existing general partner from the Tax Credit Property Partnerships and assume control only for due cause related to the nonperformance of the general partner.&#160;&#160;The Tax Credit Fund Partnerships and Tax Credit Property Partnerships, in which the Company has a substantive controlling general partner or managing member interest or in which it has concluded it is the primary beneficiary of a VIE, are being consolidated although the Company has practically no economic interest in such entities.&#160;&#160;These Tax Credit Fund Partnerships and Tax Credit Property Partnerships are included within our Consolidated Partnerships.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The analysis as to whether the entity is a VIE and whether we consolidate it is subject to significant judgment.&#160;&#160;Some of the criteria we are required to consider include, among others, determination of the degree of control over an entity by its various equity holders, design of the entity, relationships between equity holders, determination of the primary beneficiary and the ability to replace general partners.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Financial information presented for certain of the Tax Credit Fund Partnerships and Tax Credit Property Partnerships is as of September 30, 2011 and 2010 and the twelve months ended September 30, 2011 and 2010, the most recent date for which information is available.</font></div>

<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Equity Interests in Tax Credit Property Partnerships</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Tax Credit Fund Partnerships invest in low-income housing property-level partnerships that generate tax credits and tax losses.&#160;&#160;Neither we nor the Tax Credit Fund Partnerships control these Tax Credit Property Partnerships and, therefore, we do not consolidate them in our financial statements.&#160;&#160;&#8220;Equity interests in Tax Credit Property Partnerships&#8221; represents the limited partner investments in those Tax Credit Property Partnerships, which the Tax Credit Fund Partnerships carry on the equity method of accounting.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CENTERLINE HOLDING COMPANY</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The reduction for the current period is due primarily to the equity losses of $304.2 million (primarily resulting from non-cash depreciation expense) recognized in the current period, the sale of Tax Credit Property Partnerships of $5.4 million, and cash distributions of $17.3 million to the limited partners, partially offset by an increase in investment in new Tax Credit Property Partnerships of $111.2 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div align="center">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Land, Buildings and Improvements, Net</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Land, buildings and improvements are attributable to the Tax Credit Property Partnerships we consolidate as a result of gaining significant control over their general partner.&#160;&#160;Land, buildings and improvements to be held and used are carried at cost which includes the purchase price, acquisition fees and expenses, construction period interest and any other costs incurred in acquiring and developing the properties.&#160;&#160;The cost is depreciated over the estimated useful lives using primarily the straight-line method.&#160;&#160;Expenditures for repairs and maintenance are charged to expense as incurred; major renewals and betterments are capitalized.&#160;&#160;At the time of retirement and otherwise disposal, the cost (net of accumulated depreciation) and related liabilities are eliminated and the profit or loss on such disposition is reflected in earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Land, buildings and improvements are evaluated for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of such assets may not be recoverable.&#160;&#160;The determination of asset impairment is a two-step process.&#160;&#160;First, the carrying amount of the asset is deemed not recoverable if it exceeds the sum of the undiscounted cash flows and the projected cash proceeds from the eventual sale of the asset.&#160;&#160;If such estimates are below the carrying amount, the impairment loss is measured as the amount by which the carrying amount of the asset exceeds fair value, which is determined by a direct capitalization method by applying a capitalization rate obtained from market data for comparative investments to stabilized net operating income levels.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The decrease for the current period is due primarily to a $80.5 million reduction in the carrying basis of land, buildings and improvements relating to equity investments for certain properties due to impairments.&#160;&#160;The decrease for the current period also includes receivable reserve of $50.8 million between the Tax Credit Property Partnerships and the Tax Credit Fund Partnerships as a result of an increase in impairments recognized on equity investments and receivables due from the Tax Credit Property Partnerships, $8.1 million related to properties that were sold or foreclosed upon and current period depreciation of $28.4 million.&#160;&#160;This was partially offset by $57.0 million of additional properties consolidated during 2011 and net fixed asset additions of $4.5 million for certain properties.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Other expenses decreased in 2011, primarily due to a decrease of $17.3 million in the reserves against receivables due from Tax Credit Property Partnerships as well as reductions in non-recurring expenses for certain properties during 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Other losses principally represent the equity losses that Tax Credit Fund Partnerships recognize in connection with their investments in non-consolidated Tax Credit Property Partnerships.&#160;&#160;The decrease in losses during 2011 primarily resulted from a reduction of $40.4 million related to suspended losses for Tax Credit Fund Partnerships whose investment balances in certain Tax Credit Property Partnerships have reached zero, a reduction of approximately $8.6 million of losses due to properties being sold or foreclosed during 2011 and an increase of $13.5 million in recognized gains, net of losses on the sale of property investments during 2011, offset by an increase of $14.8 million in expenses recognized by certain Tax Credit Property Partnerships pertaining to the change in value of their interest rate swaps.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">On March 5, 2010, CFin Holdings entered into a Senior Secured Credit Agreement (the &#8220;CFin Holdings Credit Agreement&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the CFin Holdings Credit Agreement, we were permitted to borrow up to $20.0 million (the &#8220;Initial Loan&#8221;), plus, under certain conditions, up to an additional $1.0 million in each calendar year until March 5, 2037.&#160;&#160;We borrowed the $20 million at the time of the loan closing as required by the lender.&#160;&#160;Borrowings under the CFin Holdings Credit Agreement were secured by a first priority lien on substantially all of CFin Holdings&#8217; existing and future assets.&#160;&#160;Borrowings under the CFin Holdings Credit Agreement bore interest at a rate of 10% per annum, which was paid-in-kind and capitalized to the outstanding principal balance on the last business day of March, June, September and December of each year.&#160;&#160;Neither Centerline Holding Company nor its subsidiaries were guarantors of this facility.&#160;&#160;In June 2011, CFin Holdings repaid $20.0 million in principal amount of this facility.&#160;&#160;At that time, the credit facility commitments were terminated, and accrued and capitalized interest of $2.6 million was waived, resulting in a gain on settlement of liabilities in the amount of $2.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We refer to the Series A-3 Cumulative Preferred Shares as the &#8220;Series A Shares&#8221;.&#160;&#160;We refer to the Series B-2 Subordinate Cumulative Preferred Shares as the &#8220;Series B Shares&#8221;.&#160;&#160;We also collectively refer to the Series A Shares and the Series B Shares as the &#8220;Preferred Shares&#8221;.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Preferred Shares are subject to mandatory tender for remarketing and purchase on such dates and each remarketing date thereafter at their respective liquidation amounts plus all distributions accrued but unpaid.&#160;&#160;Each holder of the Preferred Shares will be required to tender its shares on the dates listed above, unless Equity Issuer decides to remarket them.&#160;&#160;Unless Equity Issuer has determined to redeem them, holders of the Preferred Shares may elect to retain their shares upon remarketing, with a new distribution rate to be determined at that time by the remarketing agent.&#160;&#160;After the mandatory tender date for a series, Equity Issuer may redeem the Preferred Shares of that series, subject to certain conditions.&#160;&#160;The Preferred Shares are not convertible into our Common Shares.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">If any series of Preferred Shares remains outstanding on or after May 15, 2019, the Preferred Shareholders of such series may direct Equity Issuer to sell the Series A-1 Freddie Mac certificates (discussed in Note 8) to Freddie Mac in return for the retirement of the subject series of Preferred Shares.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Preferred Shares have annual preferred dividends payable monthly in arrears upon declaration by our Board of Trustees, but only to the extent of tax-exempt net income for the particular month.&#160;&#160;With respect to payment of distributions and amounts upon liquidation, dissolution or winding-up of our Company, the Series A Shares rank, senior to:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our Series A Convertible Community Reinvestment Act Preferred Shares (&#8220;Convertible CRA Shares&#8221;) initially were intended to enable financial institutions to receive certain regulatory benefits in connection with their investment.&#160;&#160;We developed a proprietary method for allocating these regulatory benefits to specific financial institutions that invested in the Convertible CRA Shares.&#160;&#160;As a result of the December 2007 re-securitization transaction, we do not believe that these shares will continue to qualify for credits under the Community Reinvestment Act.&#160;&#160;Other than the preferred allocation of regulatory benefits, the holders of the Convertible CRA Shares receive the same economic benefits as our Common Shareholders.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Convertible CRA Shares have no voting rights, except on matters relating to the terms of the Convertible CRA Shares or to amendments to our Trust Agreement that would adversely affect the Convertible CRA Shares.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The shareholders of the Convertible CRA shares have the option to convert their shares into Common Shares on a one-for-one basis.&#160;&#160;Upon conversion, the shareholders would no longer be entitled to a special allocation of the regulatory benefit.</font></div>

<div align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Lock-Up Agreements and Series B Special Shares related to Tax Benefits Preservation Plan</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In March 2010, we entered into lock-up agreements with each of Wells Fargo Bank, NA and one of its affiliates, Bank of America, NA and certain of its affiliates, Natixis, and affiliates of TRCLP pursuant to which each of them&#160;&#160;agreed&#160;&#160;for a period of three years commencing on the date of the March 2010 Restructuring, which we refer to as the lock-up period, not to offer, sell, offer to sell, contract to sell,&#160;&#160;grant any option to purchase or otherwise sell or dispose of any of their Company equity interests or take an action that could result in a transfer or deemed a transfer of their Company equity interests, subject to certain exceptions set forth in each such lock up agreement.&#160;&#160;Each of TRCLP, Wells Fargo Bank, NA, Bank of America, NA, and Natixis also agreed not to acquire any additional Company equity interests during the lock-up period, subject to certain exceptions set forth in each such lock-up agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In addition to the lock-up agreements, our Board of Trustees adopted a Tax Benefits Preservation Plan, or Rights Plan, which, along with the lock-up agreements, is intended to preserve the utilization of our net operating loss carry forwards.&#160;&#160;Use of these carry forwards could be jeopardized if we were to have an &#8220;ownership change&#8221; as defined by Section 382 of&#160;&#160;the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Pursuant to the Rights Plan, the Company issued one Series B Share purchase right for each outstanding common share equivalent and each preferred vote share outstanding on the applicable record date, each right representing the right to purchase, upon terms and conditions set forth in the Rights Plan, one one-millionth (subject to adjustment) of a Series B Share at a price of $0.66 per such fractional share.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The rights will be distributed only if certain events were to happen that could lead to an &#8220;ownership change&#8221; resulting in a loss of net operating loss carryforwards and would be exercisable only upon distribution.&#160;&#160;Until a right is distributed and exercised, it provides no incremental economic or voting rights to the holders of the associated shares.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Each Series B Special Share purchased upon the exercise of the rights would be entitled to (i) preferential quarterly distributions; and (ii) preferential payment (in the event of our liquidation, dissolution or winding up).&#160;&#160;Each Series B Special Share would have 1,000,000 votes and would vote together with our Common Shares of beneficial interest.&#160;&#160;Finally, in the event of any merger, consolidation or other transaction in which Common Shares of beneficial interest are exchanged, each Series B Special Share would be entitled to receive 1,000,000 times the amount received per Common Share.&#160;&#160;Series B Special Shares would not be redeemable.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Rights Plan is intended to deter any potential acquirer of shares issued by the Company from acquiring shares which results in a loss of our net operating loss carryforwards and accordingly the Rights Plan may never be triggered.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<td>

</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Under our dividend reinvestment and Common Share purchase plan, Common Shareholders may elect to have their distributions automatically reinvested in additional Common Shares at a price equal to the average of the high and low market price from the previous day&#8217;s trading, and make cash payments for further investment.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, there were 125,079 shares participating in the plan, which represented 283 investors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Board of Trustees has authorized the implementation of a Common Share repurchase plan, enabling us to repurchase, from time to time, up to 3.0 million Common Shares.&#160;&#160;This plan has no expiration date.&#160;&#160;The repurchases are made in the open market and the timing is dependent on the availability of Common Shares and other market conditions.&#160;&#160;In connection with our Term Loan and Revolving Credit Facility (see Note 15), we are restricted from repurchasing our shares during the term of such facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In addition to the repurchase plan, we may repurchase shares from employees in connection with tax withholding requirements upon vesting of restricted share grants.&#160;&#160;We account for repurchased Common Shares as treasury shares of beneficial interest.&#160;&#160;These repurchases are not subject to the Term Loan and Revolving Credit Facility restrictions described above.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Instead of cash, we may, at our discretion, exchange the SCUs (and any accrued but unpaid distributions) for Common Shares on a one-for-one basis, subject to anti-dilution adjustments.&#160;&#160;We would issue the Common Shares at a price equal to the average closing market price of our Common Shares for the five consecutive trading days prior to the date when we receive notice of intent to convert.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As part of the March 2010 Restructuring, we issued a total of 19.3 million Special Series A Shares (see Note 3), resulting in a dilution of the voting rights attributable to SCU holders.&#160;&#160;Subsequent to the March 2010 Restructuring, we no longer deem the SCU holders to possess significant influence, and we no longer allocate income to the SCU holders.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During the year ended December 31, 2011, 864,229 SCUs and their respective special preferred voting shares were exchanged for the same amount of Common Shares.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Other</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As of December 31, 2011 and 2010, other minority interests represent the 10% interest in CFin Holdings owned by Natixis.&#160;&#160;Natixis has been issued a warrant which, if exercised, would increase Natixis&#8217; ownership percentage to 19%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The warrant became exercisable in June 2009 and expires in June 2012.&#160;&#160;It is callable by CCG at any time after June 28, 2011.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, the warrant is valued at $0 and was not exercised.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Some of our pre-tax income is derived from our tax-exempt investments included in our Affordable Housing Equity segment, which until July 31, 2011 were held within flow-through entities.&#160;&#160;In October 2011, the parent trust filed an Entity Classification Election with the IRS to become taxed as a corporation.&#160;&#160;Previously, the parent trust was treated as a pass-through entity and all items of income and deductions flowed through to its investors.&#160;&#160;This change in tax status resulted in the parent trust becoming subject to entity-level taxes effective July 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;On February 6, 2012 the parent trust provided investors a final schedule K-1 for the tax period beginning January 1, 2011 and ending July 30, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">On August 1, 2011 CHC filed an amended 2009 tax return resulting in the restoration of approximately $61.5 million of net operating loss carryforward and approximately $229.1 million of capital loss carryforward.&#160;&#160;This permitted a carryover (and stepped up) basis in the stock of Centerline REIT, LLC (&#8220;REIT&#8221;).&#160;&#160;With the filing of the Company&#8217;s 2010 tax return, this stepped up basis was recognized as a capital loss on the liquidation of REIT, and was utilized to offset the capital gain on the sale of a subsidiary as part of the March 2010 restructuring.&#160;&#160;The recognition and utilization of the capital loss allowed us to restore our net operating losses.&#160;&#160;Following the filing, our federal net operating loss carryforward is approximately $204.0 million, our capital loss carryforward is approximately $165.9 million and our state and local net operating loss carryforward is approximately $203.0 million.&#160;&#160;Net operating losses can be carried forward and offset taxable income for 20 years and expire in 2027 through 2030.&#160;&#160;Our capital losses can offset capital gains for 5 years and expires in 2015.&#160;&#160;Our major tax jurisdictions where we file income tax returns include Federal, New York State and City, Texas and California.&#160;&#160;The statute of limitations for the open years expires in 2012 through 2015.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As a result of the parent trust&#8217;s change in tax status from a pass-through entity to a corporation, the parent trust&#8217;s deferred tax assets and liabilities were recorded at December 31, 2011 resulting in a net increase to our deferred tax asset of $73.6 million.&#160;&#160;During 2011, we recorded a net deferred tax liability adjustment as a result of other comprehensive income, directly to equity with corresponding adjustment to the valuation allowance.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">To date, we have settled federal audits for the tax years through 2007 without any significant negative audit adjustments.&#160;&#160;The federal audit for 2008 has begun and no significant negative adjustments have been proposed thus far.&#160;&#160;In addition, we have recently begun a New York State audit for the 2008 through 2010 tax years and no significant negative adjustments have been proposed thus far.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Management has determined that, in light of the historical losses and no reasonable basis to conclude that the Company will have income for the foreseeable future, any benefit from the deferred tax assets likely will not be realized; hence, a full valuation allowance has been recorded.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Note28"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>NOTE 28 &#8211; Financial Risk Management and Derivatives</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">A.</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">General</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Company is exposed to financial risks arising from our business operations and economic conditions.&#160;&#160;We manage interest-rate risk by hedging.&#160;&#160;We evaluate our interest-rate risk on an ongoing basis to determine if it would be advantageous to engage in any additional derivative transactions.&#160;&#160;We do not use derivatives for speculative purposes.&#160;&#160;We manage liquidity risk by extending term and maturity on debt, by reducing the amount of debt outstanding, and by producing cash flow from operations.&#160;&#160;We manage credit risk by developing and implementing strong credit and underwriting procedures.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Business segment results include all direct and contractual revenues and expenses of each business segment and allocations of certain indirect expenses based on specific methodologies.&#160;&#160;These reportable business segments are strategic business units that primarily generate revenue streams that are distinctly different from one another and are generally managed separately.&#160;&#160;Transactions between business segments are accounted for as third-party arrangements for the purposes of presenting business segment results of operations.&#160;&#160;Typical intersegment eliminations include fees earned from Consolidated Partnerships and intercompany interest.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Note31"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>NOTE 31 &#8211; Commitments and Contingencies</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Yield Transactions</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Through the isolated special purpose entities described below, we have entered into several credit intermediation agreements with either Natixis or Merrill Lynch (each a &#8220;Primary Intermediator&#8221;) to provide agreed-upon rates of return to third-party investors for pools of multifamily properties in certain Tax Credit Fund Partnerships.&#160;&#160;In return, we have received, or will receive fees, generally at the start of each credit intermediation period.&#160;&#160;There are a total of 20 outstanding agreements to provide the specified returns through the construction and lease-up phases and through the operating phase of the properties.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Total potential exposure pursuant to these credit intermediation agreements at December 31, 2011 is $1.4 billion, assuming the Tax Credit Fund Partnerships achieve no return whatsoever beyond the December 31, 2011 measurement date (assuming that all underlying properties fail and are foreclosed upon, causing us to invoke the &#8220;calamity call&#8221; provision in each fund on December 31, 2011).&#160;&#160;Of these totals:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In connection with the Merrill Master Agreement, CHC entered into a Reaffirmation of Guarantee in favor of Merrill Lynch whereby under certain circumstances CHC will indemnify Merrill Lynch for losses incurred under the yield transactions to the extent these losses are caused by events that occurred prior to the execution of the Merrill Master Agreement.&#160;&#160;As part of the Merrill Master Agreement, if certain conditions are met, we have agreed to terms for the restructuring of certain bonds that were part of the December 2007 re-securitization with Freddie Mac and Merrill Lynch has agreed to allow certain assets of Guaranteed Holdings to be used for these bond restructurings.&#160;&#160;In connection with the Merrill Master Agreement, we accrued $3.0 million and $25.7 million in credit intermediation assumption fees in the years ended December 31, 2011 and 2010, respectively, included in &#8220;Accounts Payable, accrued expenses and other liabilities&#8221; on our Consolidated Balance Sheets and included in &#8220;Other Fees&#8221; within &#8220;General and Administrative Expenses&#8221; on our Consolidated Statements of Operations.&#160;&#160;The fee is due upon the termination of certain yield transactions and is calculated as 50% of the value of the collateral securing Guaranteed Holdings&#8217; obligations under these yield transactions but not to exceed $42.0 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The carrying value of all the above obligations under credit intermediation agreements, representing the deferral of the fee income over the obligation periods, was $19.5 million as of December 31, 2011 and $23.7 million as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;This amount is included in &#8220;Deferred revenues&#8221; within &#8220;Accounts payable, accrued expense and other liabilities&#8221; on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Loss Reserve Relating to Yield Transactions</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We developed a strategy to address a marked decline in the operating performance of many of the non-stabilized properties underlying our Affordable Housing investments, to manage our exposure under the yield transactions described above and to address the declining cash flows to our Series B Freddie Mac Certificates.&#160;&#160;To address these matters and their potential impact on our interests, we expect to restructure many of the mortgage revenue bonds to allow the bonds secured by these properties to stabilize.&#160;&#160;In connection with the Natixis Master Agreement and the Merrill Master Agreement, we have agreed to terms for the restructuring of certain of the mortgage revenue bonds.&#160;&#160;This strategy, including the terms agreed to in the Natixis Master Agreement and the Merrill Master Agreement, entails cash infusions, which could approximate $159.0 million, from us and other parties with an economic interest in the properties, or may result in a reduction in the principal balance of our Series B Freddie Mac Certificates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CENTERLINE HOLDING COMPANY</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font size="3">&#160;</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For many of the properties in the pools associated with the credit intermediation agreements described under &#8220;Yield Transactions&#8221; above, mortgage revenue bonds were included in the December 2007 re-securitization transaction. Certain credit intermediated funds have equity investments in the properties underlying some of the bonds that require restructuring.&#160;&#160;If the required principal buy downs are not made for these bonds, the underlying properties can be foreclosed upon which could cause a substantial recapture of LIHTCs, thereby reducing the rate of return earned by the limited partners of the funds.&#160;&#160;A reduction in the rate of return below the rate specified at inception of the investment fund would trigger a default event that could require a payment to be made by the Primary Intermediators to the limited partners of the funds.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Should the Primary Intermediators expend cash to execute these restructurings, CFin Holdings, CFin or Guaranteed Holdings may have to reimburse them or they may have to forfeit cash and other assets that we have deposited as collateral.&#160;&#160;Should the Primary Intermediators not expend cash to the extent we have projected, we could incur additional impairments of our Series B Freddie Mac Certificates.&#160;&#160;We have analyzed the expected operations of the underlying properties and, as of December, 31, 2011, we have estimated that payments by us totaling $71.9 million will need to be made in order to complete the restructuring to reduce the principal balance of mortgage debt on specified properties.&#160;&#160;This mortgage reduction will limit our exposure under the yield guarantee arrangements.&#160;&#160;Of the expected payments to be made, $32.3 million is accrued as part of &#8220;Accounts payable, accrued expenses and other liabilities&#8221; on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;The remaining $39.6 million will be funded from the stabilization escrow established in connection with the 2007 re-securitization transaction, which has been fully reserved in prior years.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the reserve for possible losses recorded in &#8220;Accounts payable, accrued expenses and other liabilities&#8221; on the Consolidated Balance Sheets was $89.4 million.&#160;&#160;In addition, the impact of the assumed restructuring led to a $78.0 million impairment of our Series B Freddie Mac Certificates in 2010 (see Notes 8 and 24).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We have not yet been called upon to make payments under the yield transaction obligations.&#160;&#160;However, certain cash and other assets were pledged as collateral to Merrill Lynch and Natixis by CFin, CFin Holdings, and Guaranteed Holdings. As of December 31, 2011, Guaranteed Holdings maintained collateral to satisfy Merrill Lynch&#8217;s collateral requirements, consisting of cash deposits of $44.7 million which are included in &#8220;Deferred costs and other assets, net&#8221; on our Consolidated Balance Sheets and a $19.3 million in investments in Series A-1 Freddie Mac Certificates included in &#8220;Available-for-sale investments&#8221; on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;In addition, as of December 31, 2011, Centerline Financial maintained a cash balance of $66.5 million included in &#8220;Cash and cash equivalents&#8221; as a capital requirement in support of its exposure under its credit intermediation agreements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Tax Credit Property Partnerships</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">To manage our exposure to risk of loss, we are able to remove the existing general partner from the Tax Credit Property Partnerships and assume control only for due cause related to the nonperformance of the general partner.&#160;&#160;We assumed these general partnership interests to preserve our direct or indirect investments in mortgage revenue bonds or the equity investments in Tax Credit Property Partnerships on behalf of Tax Credit Fund Partnerships that we manage.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We have hired qualified property managers for each of the Tax Credit Property Partnerships in order to improve the performances of these partnerships.&#160;&#160;During our holding period, we may need to support the Tax Credit Property Partnerships if they have not yet reached stabilization or we may choose to fund deficits as needed, to protect our interests.&#160;&#160;The assets continue to be actively managed to minimize the necessary cash flow outlays and maximize the performance of each asset.&#160;&#160;Due to the uncertain nature of cash needs at these Tax Credit Property Partnerships, we cannot estimate how much may ultimately be advanced while we own the general partner and co-general partner interests.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In addition, we may advance funds to Tax Credit Fund Partnerships to allow them to make supplemental loans for Tax Credit Property Partnerships in which they invest.&#160;&#160;These advances are then repaid to us from cash flows, if any, at the Tax Credit Fund Partnership level.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of our Term Loan and Revolving Credit Facility, we are, in certain cases, limited in the amount of advances that can be made.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As of December 31, 2011, we had a $64.1 million receivable for advances as described above, net of a $38.5 million reserve for bad debt (see Note 29).&#160;&#160;This includes $23.3 million (net of a $9.3 million reserve) recorded in CAHA&#8217;s books and $40.8 million (net of a $29.2 million reserve) recorded in our isolated special purpose entities&#8217; CFin Holdings and Guaranteed Holdings financial statements, including $25.1 million net receivables that were assigned by CAHA to these entities on March 5, 2010 in connection with the restructuring of the Yield Transactions as part of Receivables Assignment and Assumption Agreements with both Natixis and Merrill.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">B.</font></div>

</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As of December 31, 2011, we had commitments to sell mortgages that have already been funded to GSEs totaling $185.7 million, which are included in &#8220;Mortgage loans held for sale and other assets&#8221; on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">C.</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Mortgage Loan Loss Sharing Agreements</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Under the DUS program, we originate loans through one of our subsidiaries that are thereafter purchased or credit enhanced by Fannie Mae and sold to third party investors.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to a master loss sharing agreement with Fannie Mae, we retain a first loss position with respect to the loans that we originate and sell under this program.&#160;&#160;For these loss sharing loans, we assume responsibility for a portion of any loss that may result from borrower defaults, based on the Fannie Mae loss sharing formulas, and Fannie Mae risk Levels I, II or III.&#160;&#160;All of the 1,019 loss sharing loans in this program as of December 31, 2011, were Level I loans.&#160;&#160;For a majority of these loans, if a default occurs, we are responsible for the first 5% of the unpaid principal balance and a portion of any additional losses to a maximum of 20% of the original principal balance; any remaining loss is borne by Fannie Mae.&#160;&#160;A modified risk sharing arrangement is applied to 93 loans in which our risk share is reduced to 0% to 75% of our overall share of the loss.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to this agreement, we are responsible for funding 100% of mortgagor delinquency (principal and interest) and servicing advances (taxes, insurance and foreclosure costs) until the amounts advanced exceed 5% of the unpaid principal balance at the date of default.&#160;&#160;Thereafter, for Level I loans, we may request interim loss sharing adjustments that allow us to fund 25% of such advances until final settlement under the master loss sharing agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We also participate in loss sharing transactions under Freddie Mac&#8217;s DUI program whereby we have originated loans that were purchased by Freddie Mac.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of our master agreement with Freddie Mac, we are obligated to reimburse Freddie Mac for a portion of any loss that may result from borrower defaults in DUI transactions.&#160;&#160;For such loans, if a default occurs, our share of the standard loss will be the first 5% of the unpaid principal balance and 25% of the next 20% of the remaining unpaid principal balance to a maximum of 10% of the unpaid principal balance.&#160;&#160;The loss on a defaulted loan is calculated as the unpaid principal amount due, unpaid interest due and default resolutions costs (taxes, insurance, operation and foreclosure costs) less recoveries.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, we had 59 loss sharing loans in this program.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our maximum exposure at December 31, 2011, pursuant to these agreements, was $860.6 million (representing what we would owe in accordance with the loss sharing percentages with Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac described above if every loan defaulted and losses were incurred in amounts equal to or greater than these levels for which we are responsible), although we believe this amount is not indicative of our actual potential losses.&#160;&#160;We maintain an allowance for risk-sharing obligations for loans originated under these product lines at a level that, in management&#8217;s judgment, is adequate to provide for estimated losses.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2011 and 2010, that reserve was $21.7 million and $29.9 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;The reserve is recorded in &#8220;Accounts payable, accrued expenses and other liabilities&#8221; (see Note 17) on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">From time to time, the Company may become involved in various claims and legal actions arising in the ordinary course of business.&#160;&#160;In the opinion of management, the ultimate disposition of these matters will not have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and therefore no accrual is required as of December 31, 2011 and 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">E.</font></div>

<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Other Contingent Liabilities</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We have entered into several transactions pursuant to the terms of which we will provide credit support to construction lenders for project completion and Fannie Mae conversion.&#160;&#160;In some instances, we have also agreed to acquire subordinated bonds to the extent the construction period bonds do not fully convert.&#160;&#160;In some instances, we also provide payment, operating deficit, recapture and replacement reserve guarantees as business requirements for developers to obtain construction financing.&#160;&#160;Our maximum aggregate exposure relating to these transactions was $182.9 million as of December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;To date, we have had minimal exposure to losses under these transactions and anticipate no material liquidity requirements in satisfaction of any guarantee issued.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In addition, we have entered into a number of indemnification agreements whereby we will indemnify a purchaser of the general partner (&#8220;GP&#8221;) interests in Tax Credit Property Partnerships for unspecified losses they may incur as a result of certain acts, including those that occurred while we served as the GP.&#160;&#160;Although some of the indemnification agreements do not explicitly provide a cap on our exposure, to date we have had minimal exposure to losses under these transactions and anticipate no material liquidity requirements in satisfaction of any indemnities issued.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Centerline Financial has two credit intermediation agreements to provide for monthly principal and interest debt service payments for debt owed by Tax Credit Property Partnerships owned by third parties, to the extent there is a shortfall in payment from the underlying property.&#160;&#160;In return, we receive fees monthly based on a fixed rate until the expiration of the agreements that occur in 2023 and 2025.&#160;&#160;Total potential exposure pursuant to these transactions is $33.7 million as well as monthly interest obligations, assuming the bonds default and cannot be sold.&#160;&#160;The recourse upon default would be to acquire the bond and foreclose on the underlying property at which point the property would be rehabilitated or sold.&#160;&#160;Deferred fee income over the obligation period was $0.9 million based on the fair value of the obligations as of December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;This amount is included in &#8220;Deferred revenues&#8221; within &#8220;Accounts payable, accrued expenses and other liabilities&#8221; on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As indicated in Note 29, an affiliate of TRCLP assumed $5.0 million of the debt under our Term Loan and Revolving Credit Facility in connection with a consulting and advisory agreement we entered into with the TRCLP affiliate.&#160;&#160;Under the consulting agreement, we are obligated to pay fees to the TRCLP affiliate equal to the interest payable on the TRCLP Loan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Under the terms of the agreement and as detailed in Note 29, in some cases, if we terminate the agreement we may be obligated to immediately repay the remaining principal balance of the TRCLP loan.</font></div>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As of December 31, 2011, we had 320,291 Convertible CRA Shares outstanding.&#160;&#160;As we had not repurchased these Convertible CRA Shares as of January 1, 2012, the holders of the Convertible CRA Shares have the option to require us to purchase the Convertible CRA Shares for the original gross issuance price per share (plus accumulated and unpaid distributions), which totaled approximately $6.0 million as of December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the terms of the Credit Agreement, we are restricted from meeting this requirement.&#160;&#160;A holder (the &#8220;Convertible CRA Shareholder&#8221;) of 214,247 Convertible CRA Shares (the &#8220;Option Shares&#8221;) exercised their option to require us to purchase the Option Shares for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $4.0 million on January 4, 2012.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the option agreement, we were required to purchase the Option Shares by January 10, 2012.&#160;&#160;Due to the terms of the Credit Agreement that restrict our ability to repurchase the Option Shares, we are currently in discussions with the Convertible CRA Shareholder in an effort to settle this obligation for an amount significantly less than $4.0 million.&#160;&#160;We are also in discussions with the other remaining holder of Convertible CRA Shares to explore various ways to mitigate the above-referenced repurchase risk with respect to that holder.&#160;&#160;Due to our contractual obligations to certain former holders of our Convertible CRA Shares (the &#8220;Former CRA Holders&#8221;), the settlement of our obligations to the current holders of Convertible CRA Shares may trigger payments to the Former CRA Holders that agreed to the redemption of their Convertible CRA Shares on terms less favorable than those that are provided to the current holders of Convertible CRA Shares.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
